hook.situation: Pointing out the exact item, place, food, book, or person you mean by putting a description before the noun.
objectives: Use A-ㄴ/은 N for adjective descriptions: 작은 가방, 조용한 카페.
Use V-는 N for present or habitual action descriptions: 손님이 찾는 모델, 제가 읽는 책.
Recognize completed action modifiers that appear in real shopping talk: 어제 본 가방, 새로 들어온 물건.
hook.whyItMatters: Korean descriptions come before the noun. Once learners can build 작은 가방 and 어제 본 가방, they can identify the right thing without making several short disconnected sentences.

grammarNotes.title: A-ㄴ/은 N - an adjective describing a noun
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use the adjective modifier to make one noun precise enough for the listener to pick the right item.
grammarNotes.formation: Put the adjective form directly before the noun. Vowel-ending adjective stems usually take ㄴ: 예쁘다 becomes 예쁜 가방. Consonant-ending adjective stems take 은: 작다 becomes 작은 가방. 하다 adjectives become 한: 조용하다 becomes 조용한 카페.

examples.note: 예쁘다 becomes 예쁜 before a noun.
작다 has a consonant stem, so it takes 은.

b.en: I am looking for a small bag.

contrastPairs.explanation: 작아요 is a full sentence ending. 작은 is a modifier that must stand before a noun.
좋다 describes a state, so it becomes 좋은. 좋아하다 is a verb, so it becomes 좋아하는.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Do not put the adjective after the noun as in English. Korean modifiers come before the noun.

exceptions: 있다/없다-type descriptive words often use 는: 맛있는 음식, 재미없는 영화.
ㅂ irregular adjectives change before 은: 춥다 becomes 추운, 가볍다 becomes 가벼운.
Several modifiers can stack before one noun: 어제 본 작은 가방.

grammarNotes.title: V-는 N - a present or habitual action describing a noun
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use V-는 N when the noun is identified by an action someone or something does.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach 는 to the verb stem before the noun: 찾다 becomes 찾는 모델, 읽다 becomes 읽는 책, 먹다 becomes 먹는 음식. For ㄹ stems, drop ㄹ before 는: 살다 becomes 사는 곳.

examples.en: a model customers ask for a lot
examples.note: 찾는 describes the model by a repeated action.

examples.en: the book I am reading these days
the neighborhood where my friend lives

contrastPairs.explanation: V-는 is present or habitual. Completed actions use V-(으)ㄴ.
ㄹ stems drop ㄹ before 는: 살다 becomes 사는.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: A full sentence ending like 읽어요 cannot directly modify a noun. Change the verb into a noun modifier first.

exceptions: V-는 N does not automatically mean future. For future or intended action, Korean uses V-(으)ㄹ N: 읽을 책.
Past/completed action modifiers use V-(으)ㄴ N: 어제 본 가방, 지난주에 만난 사람.
Korean relative clauses stand before the noun, even when the English translation comes after it.

grammarNotes.title: Completed action modifiers - 어제 본 가방
grammarNotes.mentalModel: When the action already happened, Korean uses a completed modifier before the noun. This is why shop talk often says 어제 본 가방, 새로 들어온 물건, 지난주에 만난 사람.
grammarNotes.formation: For many verb stems, use ㄴ after a vowel and 은 after a consonant: 보다 becomes 본, 만나다 becomes 만난, 먹다 becomes 먹은. Irregulars and tense details expand later, but the key idea is completed action before the noun.

examples.en: the small bag I saw yesterday
examples.note: 본 is a completed action modifier, and 작은 is an adjective modifier.

examples.en: an item that newly came in
the person I met last week

a.en: the book I am reading these days

contrastPairs.explanation: Use 는 for current or habitual action, and 은/ㄴ for completed action.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: 봤어요 is a full sentence ending. To place the action before a noun, use the modifier 본.

exceptions: This chapter introduces completed modifiers only as a practical preview because they appear naturally with 어제 본 and 새로 들어온.
If the main focus is present habit, stay with V-는 N: 자주 가는 카페.

readingText.title: Finding the right bag
readingText.body: 민서는 출근할 때 들기 좋은 가방을 찾고 있었어요. 직원에게 어제 본 작은 가방이 아직 있는지 물어봤어요. 직원은 그 가방이 손님들이 많이 찾는 새로운 모델이라고 설명했어요. 안에는 필요한 물건이 꽤 많이 들어가고, 디자인도 예뻤어요. 민서는 바쁜 아침에도 들고 다니기 편한 가방이 필요했기 때문에 그 가방을 다시 한번 확인했어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo was looking for a bag that would be good to carry to work. She asked whether the small bag she saw yesterday was still available. The staff explained that it was a new model customers often ask for, and Minseo checked it again because she needed a comfortable bag for busy mornings.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서는 어떤 가방을 찾고 있었어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 출근할 때 들기 좋은 가방을 찾고 있었어요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 직원은 그 가방을 어떤 모델이라고 설명했어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 손님들이 많이 찾는 새로운 모델이라고 설명했어요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서는 왜 그 가방을 다시 확인했어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 바쁜 아침에도 들고 다니기 편한 가방이 필요했기 때문이에요.

culturalNote.title: Descriptions make requests sound clear and polite
culturalNote.body: In shops, offices, and meet-up situations, Korean often avoids a long chain of short sentences by placing the description before the noun. 어제 봤어요. 작은 가방이에요. 그거 찾고 있어요 can become 어제 본 작은 가방을 찾고 있어요, which is clearer and more natural.
culturalNote.tip: When the listener has several possible items in mind, build one precise noun phrase: 조용한 카페, 제가 읽는 책, 어제 본 작은 가방.

inlineExercises.explanation: Korean modifiers come before the noun they describe.

inlineExercises.explanation: 찾는 modifies 모델 with an action-based description.

inlineExercises.explanation: 읽어요 is a sentence ending; 읽는 modifies 책.
Adjective modifiers come before the noun.

bullets: Adjective descriptions use A-ㄴ/은 N: 예쁜 가방, 작은 지갑, 조용한 카페.
Present or habitual action descriptions use V-는 N: 찾는 모델, 읽는 책, 사는 동네.
Completed action descriptions point to a noun already affected by an action: 어제 본 가방, 새로 들어온 물건.
Best check: if the word ends like a sentence, change it before placing it in front of a noun.
